case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. (FR) Application No. 777/96, decided on 31 March 2000

clause.text: Every person has the right to apply to the Supreme Court for violations of fundamental rights.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner had the individual right under Article 17 to apply to the Supreme Court for alleged infringements of fundamental rights relating to appointments in a bank, and whether the application was time-barred or misconceived.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that the appointments of Jayawardena and Ziyard as Deputy Chief Legal Officer and Supernumerary Deputy Chief Legal Officer respectively were arbitrary, discriminatory, and violated his fundamental right to equality under Article 12(1), and sought orders to cancel those appointments.
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents argued that the application regarding Jayawardena's appointment was time-barred under Article 126(2) as it was filed well beyond one month of the alleged infringement; and that the appointment of Ziyard was a settlement benefit related to retirement, not an executive or administrative action infringing fundamental rights, thus the application was misconceived.
key_facts: Four officers (Narendrakumar, Ziyard, Jayawardena, Kiritharan) applied for one Deputy Chief Legal Officer post.
Jayawardena was selected and appointed effective 1.8.1995; Ziyard challenged this appointment in earlier proceedings.
Ziyard reached optional retirement age and was appointed Supernumerary Deputy Chief Legal Officer by court settlement on 23.10.1996.
Petitioner filed the present application on 25.11.1996 alleging infringement of Article 12(1).
The application regarding Jayawardena's appointment was filed well beyond the one-month period prescribed by Article 126(2).

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court interpreted Article 17 as granting every person the individual right to apply to the Supreme Court for infringement of fundamental rights, but emphasized that the procedural requirement under Article 126(2) imposes a strict one-month time limit to file such applications. The right to apply is personal and cannot be delayed by relying on another person's pending application.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court found the petitioner's application regarding Jayawardena's appointment was time-barred as it was filed more than one month after the petitioner became aware of the appointment. The petitioner could not rely on Ziyard's earlier application to excuse the delay. Regarding Ziyard's appointment, the Court held it was a settlement providing retiral benefits, not an executive or administrative action infringing fundamental rights, and the petitioner was not entitled to challenge it as he had not reached retirement age.
principles_established: The right to apply under Article 17 is personal and individual.
Applications under Article 126(2) must be filed within one month of the alleged infringement or imminent infringement.
Delay in filing cannot be excused by reliance on another person's application.
Settlements conferring retiral benefits do not constitute executive or administrative action infringing fundamental rights.
The maxim 'vigilantibus non dormientibus jura subveniunt' applies to fundamental rights applications.
precedents_cited: Gunawardena v. Senanayake FRD Vol. 1 p. 177
Jayawardena v. Attorney-General FRD Vol. 1 p. 175
Krishna Mining Co. Ltd. v. JEDB (1996) 2 Sri LR. 209
Gamacthige v. Siriwardena and others (1998) 1 Sri LR. 384

outcome.holding: The Court upheld the preliminary objections and dismissed the application as time-barred in respect of Jayawardena's appointment and misconceived in respect of Ziyard's appointment.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 17 establishes the petitioner's individual right to apply to the Supreme Court for fundamental rights violations, which is central to the Court's analysis of whether the petitioner had standing and timely filed the application. The Court's reasoning and dismissal hinge on the interpretation and application of this right.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Court emphasized that the right to apply under Article 17 is personal and individual, and that the petitioner could not delay filing his application relying on another's pending case. The application regarding Jayawardena was filed well beyond the one-month period, and the appointment of Ziyard was a settlement conferring retiral benefits, not an infringement of fundamental rights.
